exact_missing_items: 1. `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`
Plans/Contracts_V0.md
Add a canonical route payload / target model owner section, likely in Contracts_V0.md or an equivalent routing owner doc
define one canonical internal route/target payload for navigation
resume_url should be one serialized transport form of that payload

Add a minimal command-classification / normalization contract to the command-definition layer: `command_kind` (shell_view | navigation_wrapper | domain_action); optional `normalization` with `kind` (wrapper | deprecated_alias) and exactly one target field: `normalizes_to_contract` for wrappers OR `alias_of_command_id` for deprecated aliases
Keep wrapper metadata contract-level and narrow: point to the canonical primitive family; do not restate route payload structure there
Deprecated alias metadata should remain explicit and separate because it implies lifecycle/removal expectations that wrapper commands do not have.

Extend `GATE-010` to verify: wrapper commands marked as normalizing to the same primitive do not diverge in handler semantics unexpectedly; deprecated aliases resolve to real canonical command IDs; normalization metadata is internally consistent with the command kind
Add an explicit command-catalog pattern for: canonical command, wrapper command, deprecated alias, migration rule
Reuse the event-side alias discipline from Contracts_V0.md as the template for command deprecation/migration rules rather than inventing a weaker prose-only pattern
Event contracts already have a recognizable alias/migration pattern, but command contracts do not
Add explicit route validation rules to Contracts_V0.md.
State that invalid route payloads are contract failures, not 'best effort' cases.
Normalize before route construction, not during late destination-specific handling.

Canonical route validation rules are: reject when project_id is missing; reject when no primary selector exists; reject when both subject_id and object_kind/object_id are supplied as competing primary selectors; reject when object_kind is present without object_id; reject when object_id is present without object_kind; reject when inspector_target is present but no object selector exists; reject when tab_id conflicts with target_kind; reject when line or range appears in route_target; reject when per-surface state appears in route_target.
Add requested_account_id?, effective_account_id?, execution-scope fields, and actor_kind / execution_role to the shared runtime identity bundle and to the bridged-provider envelope
Replace tier-era persisted names/values in Prompt_Pipeline.md and Personas.md before they become entrenched in durable records
Define a canonical switch-history / pressure-episode family and make it queryable from History, Ledger, Usage, and Account/Usage Pressure projections
Add a canonical role enumeration and apply it consistently to role-scoped account policies, Persona resolution, permission scoping, and provider dispatch
Re-scope permission session cache / reject cascade and OpenCode SSE/session isolation rules to actor/lane-aware boundaries
Add scoped-identity resolver rules to Contracts_V0.md.
Keep scoped runtime families object-first and resolver-backed.
Do not add family-specific top-level route fields just because some ids are only unique within run scope.

Scoped identity rules: blocked_episode (object_id=blocked_sequence, resolver scope requires focused_run_id + node membership); scheduler_pass (requires focused_run_id); safe_point (requires focused_run_id); remediation (object_id=remediation_root_id, requires focused_run_id); attempt (object_id=attempt_id, requires focused_run_id).
Attention item rollup rules must be specified: when can N concern records collapse into one attention item, what is the severity-merge strategy, when must distinct items remain separate
Attention item disclosure rules must be specified: which items are shown inline on surfaces vs surfaced only on click vs hidden until the user navigates to the attention center
Routing rules from attention item to primary/secondary action surfaces must be specified
Canonical event families must be shared between the runtime and UI projections — the Orchestrator must NOT invent a shadow event language separate from the runtime event model
Canonical handoff/retry memory must be stored as structured runtime records NOT loose markdown; worker-facing handoff = synthesized bounded packet derived from canonical records
